executive_assessment.text: Named observations distinguish two Nadym permafrost-monitoring sites, 2024 agricultural precipitation anomalies in the Southern/North Caucasus districts and reported Yakutia fire response.

The government's 2025 plans mention Indigenous livelihoods and Moscow infrastructure, while an abstract describes Yamal-Nenets sectoral implementation. These do not establish community-level outcomes.

War/sanctions-related climate-policy context is retained with abstract-level limits. Transition-risk stress tests are conditional financial scenarios, not observed physical damage or climate-caused conflict.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2025 reports: For two monitored sites in Nadym district, Roshydromet reports positive active-layer-thickness trends of 58 and 45 cm per decade over 2005–2024.

Source dated 2025 reports: Spring-cereal growing-season precipitation in 2024 was 36% below its 1991–2020 normal in the Southern District and 30% below in the North Caucasus; local soil drought was possible in both during June–August.
Source dated 2025 reports: EMERCOM records May 2024 natural fires over more than 44,271 ha in Yakutia; 2,728 emergency-system personnel and 187 equipment units were mobilized.
Source dated 2025-09 reports: The submission reports Moscow prioritizing electricity, heating and gas-network upgrades, alongside planting wind- and frost-resistant trees and increasing irrigation.
Source dated 2026-04-17 reports: In Yamal-Nenets, adaptation is implemented mainly through sectoral plans embedded in infrastructure, civil protection and resource-management programmes.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 15 of 16 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
No directly inspected Russia-specific evidence established a climate-to-violent-conflict or climate-to-armed-conflict pathway; this is a search gap, not evidence of absence.

Roshydromet's active-layer trends are based on a small, uneven set of permafrost plots; the report says long-term trend estimation requires multi-decade records and some eastern regions lack comparable observations.
The HSE article was used at abstract level only; its broad southwest/northeast/southeast patterns do not name federal subjects and its heuristic rankings are not quantified damage estimates.
The FNI full article was not inspected; the publisher abstract supports only high-level claims about regional policy and its Yamal-Nenets case.
The 2025 Second NDC reports a second-stage adaptation plan running through 2025; post-2025 plan status and implementation were not verified.
EMERCOM 2024 readiness counts and incident figures are historical administrative records, not climate-attribution evidence; aggregate readiness does not identify weaker individual regions.
The Bank of Russia webpage summarizes stress tests and a survey, but underlying methods, sample sizes and local variation were not reviewed.
War/sanctions policy context is a bounded reverse-direction observation, not a complete pathway showing interrupted adaptation delivery.
Regional and Arctic examples are not representative household-level vulnerability assessments; Indigenous livelihood protection appears as an objective, not delivered results.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
